To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
triiodothyronine increases mitochondrial ATP production by oxidative but not glycoytic muscle in rats.
thyroid hormones increase ATP production by skeletal muscle mitochondria despite increased expression of uncoupling proteins 2 and 3.
T(3), which increases mitochondrial ATP production and mitochondrial-encoded transcripts in oxidative muscles, also increases uncoupling proteins in both oxidative and glycolitic muscles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of thyroid hormones on mitochondrial function and energy production in different types of muscle.
the role of the thyroid hormone triiodothyronine in the regulation of skeletal muscle mitochondrial function.
how thyroid hormone affects mitochondrial function and energy balance in muscle and liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T(3)-induced mitochondrial biogenesis is not a global phenomenon, and it is tissue dependent.
thyroid hormones stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis and ATP production, but this is not a universal response, as some tissues may be resistant to this effect.
T3 increases oxidative enzymes and ATP production in oxidative muscles, but does not affect ATP production in glycolytic muscles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T(3)-induced increases in mitochondrial enzymes and ATP production in oxidative tissues are independent of changes in uncoupler expression and activity.

T(3)-induced mitochondrial biogenesis in oxidative muscle is accompanied by a large increase in UCP2 and UCP3, but that the increase in UCP is insufficient to uncouple oxidative phosphorylation and decrease ATP production.
the effects of T(3), at least on Mito ATP production, are tissue specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that

T(3)-induced increases in UCP2 and UCP3 do not uncouple mitochondria and impair ATP production in oxidative tissues, despite the fact that T(3)'s effects on UCP2 and 3 are similar to the effects of uncoupling agents such as 2,4-dinitrophenol.
T(3), which increases O(2)/nutrient flux through mitochondria, does not increase ATP production in glycolytic muscles.
T(3)-induced increases in mitochondrial enzymes and ATP production are not accompanied by increases in uncoupling, at least in the rodent model we used.
